title: {Le Français en Chiffres}
description: Fascinating statistics and linguistic facts about French - from phonemes to pangrams!

sections.heading: French Sounds - Phonology
sections.text: French has 36-37 distinct sounds (phonemes) - 16 vowels and 20-21 consonants
sections.example: 4 nasal vowels (ã, ẽ, õ, {œ̃}) - unique to French! No 'th' sound (why 'the' is hard). Uvular 'r' (back of throat).

sections.heading: Syllable-Timed Language
sections.text: Each syllable gets equal time - unlike English which stresses certain words
sections.example: French flows smoothly with even rhythm. No word stress like English! Emphasis on last syllable of phrases. Creates musical, flowing sound.

sections.heading: Speaking Speed
sections.text: French speakers talk fast! 7.0-8.0 syllables per second vs English 6.5
sections.example: French needs more syllables to convey same info (lower information density), so speakers compensate by speaking faster!

sections.heading: The Alphabet & Accents
sections.example: Letters: same as English. Accents: {é è ê ë à ù û ç. Ligatures}: œ ({cœur}), æ ({rare}). {Total}: {33 unique characters!}

sections.heading: Vocabulary Size
sections.text: 100,000 words in common use - educated speakers know 30,000 actively
sections.example: {Le Grand Robert dictionary}: 100,000 words, 350,000 definitions. Average person: 5,000-30,000 words depending on education.

sections.heading: French Influence on English
sections.text: 29% of English vocabulary comes from French (thanks to Norman Conquest 1066!)
sections.example: 45% of English has Latin/French origins total. Beef, pork, royal, justice, parliament - all from French!

sections.heading: Grammar Complexity
sections.text: 2 genders, 17-20 verb tenses, ~350 irregular verbs (only ~50 common)
sections.example: Masculine/Feminine. 3 verb groups (-er, -ir, -re) + irregulars. ~25 '{essential}' irregular verbs to memorize. SVO word order like English.

sections.heading: Global Ranking
sections.text: 5th most spoken, 2nd most studied, 3rd language of business
sections.example: 300M speakers (2023), projected 700M by 2050. Official in 29 countries. One of 6 UN languages. Growing fast in Africa!

sections.heading: Fun Language Facts
sections.text: Quirky and interesting trivia about French
sections.example: Longest word: '{anticonstitutionnellement}' (25 letters). Most common word: '{de}'. Most common letter: 'e' (15%). No word for 'home' or '{shallow}'!

sections.heading: Liaison & Flow
sections.text: Words link together smoothly - consonants connect to following vowels
sections.example: '{les enfants}' sounds like 'lay-zahn-fahn' (z sound links). '{un homme}' = '{uh-nom}'. Creates beautiful flowing speech!

sections.heading: {L'Académie Française}
sections.text: Official authority on French language since 1635 - protects '{purity}' of French
sections.example: 40 immortals (lifetime members) decide official French. Resist English words. Prefer '{ordinateur}' to '{computer}', '{courriel}' to '{email}'.

sections.heading: Perfect French Pangram
sections.example: '{Portez ce vieux whisky au juge blond qui fume}' (Bring this old whisky to the blonde judge who smokes)
